miles: Hi all, new hire here. Running through onboarding and hit a snag: `make dev` starts Postgres but migrations fail with:

``nFATAL:  database files are incompatible with the server
DETAIL: The database cluster was initialized by PostgreSQL version 13, but the server is running version 14.
```

Container cycles and never reaches ready. I'm on an M1 Mac and cloned the repo from someone on Intel. Is there a low-risk way to reset the local DB but keep the seeds I added?

irina: Welcome! :wave: That message usually means the data directory was created by a different PG version or an image built for a different CPU arch. If you don't need the previous data, the fastest fix is removing the named volume so compose can create a fresh cluster.

sam: If you want a safety copy, snapshot the volume first. Example command to tar the named volume out to your cwd:

``n# replace project_postgres_data with your volume name
docker run --rm -v project_postgres_data:/data -v $PWD:/out alpine sh -c "cd /data && tar -cf /out/pgdata-backup.tar ."
```

We also have `dev/backup_local_db.sh` in the repo that wraps this if you prefer.

irina: My usual steps: 1) `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml down` 2) `docker volume rm project_postgres_data` (confirm the name first) 3) `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d postgres` 4) `make dev` (migrations/seed will run). If your compose binds a host folder (e.g., `./tmp/pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`) move that folder aside instead.

devops-bot: Note: Apple Silicon sometimes pulls arm64 images; if you accidentally used amd64 emulation you can see mismatches. See internal doc: https://redwood.dev/internal/dev-setup#arm-m1 for recommended images and compose tips.

miles: Thanks! I ran `docker volume ls` and saw `project_postgres_data` and `project_redis_data`. I backed up the postgres volume with the tar trick, removed `project_postgres_data`, and restarted compose. Migrations/seed ran cleanly. All set now :tada:
